newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile stocks end firm, boosted by foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Chile stocks end firm, boosted by foreign demand.

text.p: Chilean stocks closed firmer in line with other markets in Latin America with demand from abroad propelling regional bourses higher, said traders.
The bolsa is seen dipping lower at the opening but are likely to recover towards the close despite the holiday in the United States Friday, they said.
"Traders know there will be buyers in the U.S. Monday so there'll be no drop here," said one broker.
The 40-share .IPSA index closed up 1.06 percent at 136.64 points. The general .IGPA index gained 0.64 percent to 5,845.68 points amid turnover of 13.9 billion pesos.
Traders noted heavy demand abroad for Latin American stocks with investors drawn by the prospect of strong economic growth in most countries in the region.
"In general the whole region's looking rosy. Asian markets have been lagging this year which has helped Latin bolsas," said one trader.
In Chile, he noted selective buying in second tier stocks, such as forestry firm Masisa, which have not risen in line with the bolsa's recent rally.
Winners included bottler Andina which climbed on news of sharp increases in sale volumes in Chile and Argentina in the second quarter of the year, said dealers.
Andina, which also rallied sharply Wednesday, closed up 4.88 percent at 1,500 pesos.
Other gainers included power investment company Enersis, up two percent at 306 pesos and paper-maker CMPC which rose 1.35 percent at 5,250 pesos.
Losers included winery Concha y Toro, down 1.13 percent at 262 pesos and drug producer LabChile which shed 0.2 percent at 559 pesos.
